## Purpose
Registers the `html_render` Validator capability, which runs a single-file HTML prototype in headless Chromium and flags console errors, uncaught exceptions, and dead/uncovered navigation links as validation issues during the prototype build loop.

## Shape
- `HtmlRenderValidator` (`@register("validator", "html_render", ...)`) — the registered `Validator`; its `validate(target)` reaches the heavy Playwright check only through `target.runner.render_check(target.path)`, never importing the kernel directly.
- `render_coverage_status(result, require_render)` — resolves whether the render ran, was skipped-and-allowed, or was skipped-and-blocked (from the imported `agents.capabilities.validators.severity` module), driving whether a skip becomes a P0 or a silent pass.
- `_record_skip(target, result)` — writes a distinct `validator_skipped` audit row via the handle's `record_validation_result`, guarded so a missing runner/record hook never aborts the validator.
- Uses the single canonical `map_severity`/`render_coverage_status` imports rather than defining its own severity mapping.

## Why this shape
The module docstring is explicit about two constraints it's satisfying: it lives app-side (not kernel-side) because Playwright/Chromium is a heavy app dependency, and it only imports the kernel-side `Validator` port and `@register` decorator (the "import-linter-LEGAL" app→capabilities direction) while reaching the actual render check through a `KernelServices` handle so there is no kernel→app import edge; the offline degrade (`available=False` → no issues) is likewise a deliberate parity choice to match the legacy build loop's behavior when Chromium is unavailable.
